articles.title: Grootste politieactie ooit voor lokale politie LRH: 10 arrestaties en cannabisplantages met 1.300 planten ontmanteld in Limburg
articles.snippet: De lokale recherche van de politiezone Limburg Regio Hoofdstad (LRH) heeft deze week een omvangrijk crimineel drugsnetwerk blootgelegd. Meer dan 160 politiemensen voerden dinsdagochtend huiszoekingen uit op 18 verschillende adressen. De balans: 10 arrestaties, 9 aanhoudingen, 14 kilogram drugs, 2 actieve cannabisplantages en 300.000 euro cash geld. Opvallend: de hele operatie begon maanden geleden met een schijnbaar banale verkeerscontrole.

articles.title: Slip sliding away: football season-ticket holders fear falling down pecking order
articles.snippet: It is a symbol of the connection between the fanbase and club, but there is a growing fear executives would prefer stadiums full of one-off tourists The document known as “the oldest football season ticket in the world” promises its bearer access to every Burnley home game of the 1884-85 season. It is a ticket that predates the Football League by four years, with all the fixtures played against east Lancashire neighbours. All the same, the legend on the ticket carries a stern warning: “This card is not transferable. articles.title: London buses in decline? Why public transport in global cities is slowing to a crawl – visualised
articles.snippet: As experts fear for future of UK capital’s bus network, some commuters are giving up entirely. London is not alone – with worrying implications for the poorest in society Experts warn that slower buses risk driving passengers away: research cited by Transport for London (TfL) suggests a 10% fall in speed leads to a 6% drop in demand. Passenger journeys in London have already fallen by more than 300m a year, or 16%, since 2013, despite the city’s population growing by almost a million people. Continue reading...

articles.title: Mum’s Alzheimer’s has trapped the kids’ NatWest cash
articles.snippet: A First Saver account was set up by my mother when the children were born which we planned to use to fund them through university My mother set up NatWest First Saver accounts for my children when they were born. The accounts are held in trust for when they turn 18 and my parents have paid into them monthly to help fund them through university. My mother is now in the final stages of Alzheimer’s and I have registered financial power of attorney for her. Continue reading...

articles.title: As Japan swelters, farmers turn to new heat-resistant rice varieties to boost staple crop
articles.snippet: New rice varieties give hope that farmers can overcome the climate emergency and a warmer future that threatens harvests When schoolchildren in Shiroishi were enlisted to plant rice seedlings in June, Shinto priests blessed the land and asked the deities for a bountiful crop. Judging by the fields behind farmer Haruki Kawasaki, their prayers have been answered. The 63-year-old is preparing to harvest this year’s crop of hinatamaru , a variety of rice whose plump grains have thrived despite exposure to another hot and dry summer, conditions that typically punish rice yields. Continue reading...
